object_description: asymmetrical U-shaped volume with stepped rooftop houses
design_condition: The building aligns with the natural terrain in successive stages, spares the existing trees, responds to neighboring building fronts, and forms a sequence of courtyards, gardens, a pedestrian connection and a roof terrace.

positive.statement: The orthogonal U-shaped layout spares the group of trees while creating a gesture of entry at the center.
The two asymmetrical wings respond to the gap between neighboring fronts and open a perspective along the oblique axis.
The secondary rooftop volumes produce a lively but not excessive silhouette and a welcome visual break for the rear buildings.
The landscape concept creates a clear sequence of courtyards, a transverse pedestrian connection, a linear garden and a roof terrace.
The cross section aligns well with the natural terrain and modifies it little.
The section hierarchically distributes public, teaching and administrative areas in a clear volumetric arrangement.
The project is characterized by great accuracy in taking account of the site's urban-planning and landscape data.

negative.statement: The successive spatial layers generate an air gap and visual escape but somewhat weaken the center of the building.
The typologies and spatial organization are schematic and less accomplished than the organization of the section.
The interior of the attics lacks spatial structure.
